parsed.title: Discussion on tax filing, domain purchase, and low‑profit app ideas

topics.title: Tax filing process and potential shortcuts

claims.text: Paying 500 UAH to aunt Sveta can reduce the large main‑penalty caused by mis‑declared columns.
The author's inspector approved declarations without review for 1.5 years and was later reprimanded, prompting a full re‑check of all years' declarations.
Using Sveta’s help allowed a correct re‑declaration that cost about 1 000 UAH instead of paying all fines.
The tax calculation procedure typically takes about an hour with Excel, or up to a day for quarterly reports.

topics.title: Domain purchase as a funding source

claims.text: Someone needs to buy a calculator so there will be money for a domain.
Participant P4 is skeptical about buying a domain, calling the idea “sick” and unsuitable.

topics.title: Low profitability of a simple web/app product

claims.text: Web platforms are the simplest but far less profitable than Android/iOS apps.
SEO for the web product is poor; the site does not appear even on the 10th Google page.
There is no external traffic from social platforms, no contextual ads, and app stores promote new apps automatically.
User retention is near zero because a paywall appears within the first 10 seconds before the product can demonstrate value.
Conversion is assumed to be zero; the product does not significantly simplify anything nor integrate with banks or tax cabinets.
Successful cases involve very fast delivery (under a week) using a cross‑platform stack like Flutter and copying popular ideas with minor tweaks.
The discussed calculator works only with a UAH‑based FOP; the author had to convert all transactions using the day's exchange rate.
A bundle is sold with a 100 % discount promo code stored locally, making the password easy to find.
Participants joke about hacking the LinkedIn audience to obtain the password.
The bundle is described as a “local‑first app” with USD/UAH rate updated every 5 minutes, but the paid features actually reside in the bundle.
Someone calls the project a “free vibe‑code” with little sense, suggesting only technically knowledgeable people will try to find the password.
